title: Study on Prostate Salvage Using High-dose-rate Brachytherapy
official: Multicenter Prospective Observational Study on Prostate Salvage Using High-dose-rate Brachytherapy
summary: A prospective, observational, multicenter study analyzing salvage treatment for prostate cancer-diagnosed via next-generation imaging (choline positron emission tomography (PET)/prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)) and positive biopsy-using two fractions of high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age over 18 years.
* Patients diagnosed with local recurrence confirmed by next-generation imaging and a positive biopsy.
* Hormone-sensitive patient.
* Patients whose initial treatment consisted of brachytherapy alone, external beam radiotherapy, or external beam radiotherapy with a prostate brachytherapy boost.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Metastatic disease.
* Castration-resistant prostate cancer, defined according to EAU (European Association of Urology) guidelines: A patient who progresses despite maintaining testosterone levels within the castration range (testosterone \<50 ng/dL or \<1.7 nmol/L) and presents with at least one of the following factors: Three consecutive rises in PSA (Prostate-Specific Antigen) levels, measured one week apart, representing two increases of 50% above the nadir, with a PSA level \>2; PSA progression despite successive hormonal manipulations; Progression of bone lesions: progression or appearance of two or more bone lesions, or soft-tissue progression according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST criteria).
